clue.text: Need some grip over tyrant

indicators.note: 'some' takes only part of the following run of words, so the answer sits inside them

blocks.note: read straight across the word breaks

explanation.surface: A subject must loosen the grip a tyrant holds over him.
explanation.definitionFit: Need in the sense of want or destitution is a synonym for being poor.

clue.text: Giant of giants, really enormous initially

indicators.note: 'initially' asks for the opening letter of each of the words it follows

blocks.note: the first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A description of the biggest of all the giants.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a fairy-tale giant who is really enormous.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a man-eating giant of folklore and fairy tales.

clue.text: Dog riding sheep

blocks.note: a mutt is a mongrel dog
riding on top of, so ON

explanation.surface: A sheepdog has jumped on a sheep's back for a ride.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'riding' puts ON beneath the dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Mutton is the meat of an adult sheep, and an old word for the animal itself.

clue.text: Theory shows obsession about family

indicators.note: 'about' means going around, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: having a thing about something is an obsession
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: A psychological theory says someone is obsessed with their family.
explanation.walkthrough: To have a thing about something is an idiom for being fixated on it, which is how 'obsession' becomes a word meaning object.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's thinking on a subject is their reasoning or theory about it.

clue.text: In casual manner, friend currently playing well?

blocks.note: a player who is playing well at present is in form
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A sports fan chats casually about a mate who is on a good run.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'in form' is a loose way of saying currently playing well.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something informally means doing it without ceremony, in a relaxed way.

clue.text: Creation of TS Eliot, ladies and gentlemen

indicators.note: something created from these letters is a new thing made by rearranging them

blocks.note: the poet's name used as letters

explanation.surface: It sounds like the poet T S Eliot inventing the characters Ladies and Gentlemen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ladies' and 'Gentlemen' are the signs on the doors of public conveniences.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladies and gentlemen are the two kinds of public lavatory, signed by those words.

clue.text: Accomplishment pocketing gross pay

indicators.note: to pocket something is to take it inside, so one word holds the other

blocks.note: a coup is a notable success
'gross!' and 'ugh!' are both exclamations of disgust

explanation.surface: Someone's big achievement is pocketing a fat gross salary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gross' looks like a before-tax figure, but it is the slang cry of disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: To cough up is an informal idiom for paying money reluctantly.

clue.text: God leads boy to embrace origin of Holy Ghost

indicators.note: 'leads' puts the first item in front of the second
the origin of a word is its first letter
to embrace something is to hold it within your arms

blocks.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild
a common boy's name
first letter of Holy

explanation.surface: A religious scene of a deity and a boy hugging the Holy Ghost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holy Ghost' looks like one phrase, but only Holy is wordplay and Ghost is the definition; H goes into PAN after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A phantom is an apparition or spectre, the same as a ghost.

clue.text: On top shelf perhaps, thinner pen

blocks.note: something on the top shelf is high up
thinner, as in less heavy or dense

explanation.surface: A slimmer pen is kept up on the top shelf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks the top shelf as just one example of being high.
explanation.definitionFit: A highlighter is a broad felt-tip pen used to mark text in bright colour.

clue.text: User of feet, flat

blocks.note: first meaning: someone walking
second meaning: dull, uninspired

explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' tempts as a home or a level surface; here it means lacking life.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for a walker and an adjective for something dull and prosaic.

clue.text: Single: piece of vinyl, nostalgic looking back

indicators.note: a piece of the words is a part of them, so the answer lies inside
looking back means reading from right to left

blocks.note: the letters spanning the end of one word and start of the next

explanation.surface: A music fan pulls out an old single on vinyl, feeling nostalgic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Single' and 'vinyl' suggest a record, but Single just means sole or alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Only as an adjective means sole, the single one of its kind.

clue.text: Where salt may be taken, if necessary?

blocks.note: first meaning, a joke: salt is added to food a small fingerful at a time
second meaning: in an emergency, when needed

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is whimsical: salt is measured in pinches, so it is taken by the pinch.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in an emergency or when strictly needed, the same as if necessary.

clue.text: Unfortunately I step on it, a plant with brightly coloured leaves

indicators.note: an unfortunate outcome is one where things went wrong, so the letters are muddled

blocks.note: the letters of these words

explanation.surface: Someone apologises for treading on a colourful houseplant.
explanation.definitionFit: The poinsettia is a Christmas plant prized for its red bracts, which look like petals but are leaves.

clue.text: At home with partner, one’s inside

blocks.note: being in means being at home
a mate is a partner

explanation.surface: Someone stays at home with their partner, cosily indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inside' is slang for in prison, so 'one's inside' is one who is locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: An inmate is a prisoner, someone who is inside in the slang sense.

clue.text: Near feeling of excitement consuming a winger

indicators.note: consuming something takes it inside, so one piece swallows another

blocks.note: nigh is an old word for near
a tingle is a thrill
taken as written

explanation.surface: A football fan gets excited as a winger closes in on goal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winger' sounds like a footballer, but it is any creature with wings, here a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The nightingale is a songbird, and as a bird it is a winged creature.

clue.text: Tough second book

blocks.note: tough as in difficult or firm
to second a motion is to back it

explanation.surface: A sequel that is a hard read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like a number or a unit of time, but it is the verb meaning support.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardback is a book bound in stiff covers, as opposed to a paperback.

clue.text: Permission from Indian state leader

blocks.note: Goa is a small state on India's west coast
a head is a leader

explanation.surface: Approval granted by the chief minister of an Indian state.
explanation.definitionFit: The go-ahead is the signal that one may proceed, i.e. approval.

clue.text: Nicked, pop getting cut, hurt

indicators.note: being cut means losing a part, here the final letter

blocks.note: pop without its last letter
ached means hurt

explanation.surface: Dad was arrested and injured after being slashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nicked' tempts as cut or arrested, but here it means stolen; poach is to take game or staff illicitly.
explanation.definitionFit: To poach is to steal or take unlawfully, so poached is a synonym of stolen.

clue.text: Cat more unlikely to impress us

indicators.note: 'unlikely' suggests the letters are not in their likely order
to impress is to press something in, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: the letters of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cat that is unlikely ever to win us over.
explanation.definitionFit: A mouser is a cat valued for catching mice.

clue.text: Draw ring circled by the pony, lamely

indicators.note: moving lamely is moving awkwardly, so the letters are jumbled
circled by means surrounded, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: the letters of these words
a ring is O-shaped

explanation.surface: A lame pony plods round a show ring that has been drawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw' is a noun here: something that attracts people.
explanation.definitionFit: A honeypot is a place or thing that attracts crowds, just as a draw does.

clue.text: Rubbish untidy, natural state

indicators.note: something rubbish is broken or poor, so these letters need putting right

blocks.note: the letters of the word

explanation.surface: Mess and rubbish strewn about is the natural state of a room.
explanation.definitionFit: Nudity is being naked, the state in which people are born, hence natural.

clue.text: Opportunity destroyed

blocks.note: first meaning: a chance or attempt
second meaning: ruined, worn out

explanation.definitionFit: The word is a noun for an attempt or chance and an informal adjective for something ruined.

clue.text: Solid block stuffed with stewed dates, crisp food

indicators.note: stewing breaks food down and mixes it, so the letters are rearranged
something stuffed has another thing packed inside it

blocks.note: a brick is a solid block
the letters of the word

explanation.surface: A recipe for a dense loaf filled with cooked dates.
explanation.definitionFit: A breadstick is a long thin stick of crunchy baked dough, a crisp snack.

clue.text: Realise it’s a bit of wood

blocks.note: first meaning: to understand suddenly
second meaning: a small shoot from a tree

explanation.walkthrough: The first meaning is informal British slang for catching on.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for grasping an idea and a noun for a small branch.

clue.text: Artist in diva upset about rhetoric, ultimately

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters are thrown into a new order
ultimately points at the end, so only the last letter is kept
about means around, so the jumble goes round the other piece

blocks.note: the letters of these words
last letter of rhetoric

explanation.surface: An artist works inside a temperamental diva who is upset about some rhetoric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci was the Renaissance painter of the Mona Lisa.

clue.text: Forward, picket

blocks.note: first meaning: an attacking player in football
second meaning: a worker on strike

explanation.definitionFit: A striker is a football forward and also a worker taking industrial action, who may picket.
